summary: The US-Iran war has escalated across multiple fronts, with US strikes confirmed on Iranian civilian targets in Sirik and Kohestak, while Iran's military threatens faster and more crushing retaliation against any Israeli aggression. Hezbollah's last stronghold at Mount Ali Taher has fallen to the Israeli army, with 70-100 Hezbollah members and Iranian Quds Force advisors reportedly trapped in underground tunnels. Gulf states are experiencing severe economic disruption, with Dubai airport traffic down 31% and hotel occupancy at 56%, while the Strait of Hormuz remains a central flashpoint with South Korea preparing military deployment and Iran refusing to reopen it without lifting US sanctions.
key_points: US strikes hit a wedding ceremony in Sirik, southern Iran, killing a 4-year-old child, and a separate strike on Kohestak was confirmed as a direct hit by a US munition (Source: @presstv/205485).

IDF achieved operational control of Mount Ali Taher above and below ground, clearing militants; Hezbollah's last stronghold including the underground Imad 4 facility fell to Israeli forces (Source: @inon_yttach/10014).

70-100 Hezbollah members including Iranian Quds Force advisors are trapped in tunnels around Ali Taher heights, with Iran and Hezbollah prioritizing evacuation but facing increasing difficulty (Source: @mamlekate/104313).

Gulf states face severe economic impact from the war: Dubai airport traffic down 31%, hotel occupancy at 56%, luxury real estate sales down 59%, F1 Bahrain and Saudi esports World Cup delayed or cancelled (Source: @kianmeli1/91513).

Iran's military spokesperson stated that destroyed enemy air defenses in the 40-day war opened missile and drone routes toward occupied territories, and pledged preemptive operations wherever threatened (Source: @SharghDaily/181805).

US officials told intermediaries Washington wants to fully open the Strait of Hormuz regardless of Iran-Oman negotiations, while Iran insists it will not reopen until US embargo is lifted (Source: @naya_foriraq/89353).

South Korea reversed its position and is preparing to deploy military equipment including a maritime patrol aircraft or logistics ship to the Strait of Hormuz to support freedom of navigation (Source: @kianmeli1/91515).
US VP JD Vance stated the US will not talk to Iran unless Iran stops firing at international shipping and trade routes (Source: @yediotnews25/134648).

Satellite imagery shows an apparent impact scar at Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan dated September 2, matching Iran's September 1 attack claim, with fresh repair work observed by September 3 (Source: @shin_persian/9445).
ISIS claimed targeting an IRGC-backed PMU/Hashed Al Sha'abi vehicle in the Anbar desert in Iraq (Source: @shin_persian/9438).
A Revolutionary Guard ambush on Kurdish separatist forces occurred on the Iraq-Iran border in Kurdistan region (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/388800).

The US ambassador to Lebanon conveyed Israeli criticism of the Lebanese army's performance, demanding extensive weapons searches across south Lebanon or risking harder withdrawal terms (Source: @pkpoi/143837).
At least five US fighter jets were reported active in the region according to simultaneous reports (Source: @rodast_omiddana/80294).
Iran's FM Araghchi challenged Jordan's foreign minister on how long Iran should wait before responding to an aggressor who disrespects Arab sovereignty (Source: @presstv/205484).
A stabbing attempt near Shechem Gate in Jerusalem's Old City was neutralized by border police, with no casualties among forces (Source: @yediotnews25/134650).
The Lebanese army warned of a war remnant explosion in Froun town at 2:35, and fire was reported around Bani Hiyan (Source: @redlinkleb/40654, @rasedal3ado138e/388795).

sections.executive_summary: The US-Iran war has expanded into a multi-front conflict with confirmed US strikes on Iranian civilian targets in Sirik and Kohestak, while Iran's military pledges faster and more crushing retaliation against any Israeli aggression. Hezbollah's last stronghold at Mount Ali Taher has fallen to the Israeli army, with 70-100 Hezbollah members and Iranian Quds Force advisors reportedly trapped in underground tunnels. The Strait of Hormuz remains a central flashpoint as Iran refuses to reopen it without lifting US sanctions, while South Korea has reversed its position and is preparing military deployment to ensure freedom of navigation.
iran: US strikes confirmed on a wedding ceremony in Sirik, southern Iran, resulting in the death of a 4-year-old child, and a separate strike on Kohestak confirmed by Reuters analysis as a direct hit by a US munition (Source: @presstv/205485, @presstv/205486).

Iran's military spokesperson stated that the destruction of enemy air defense systems during the 40-day war opened missile and drone routes toward occupied territories, and pledged preemptive operations wherever a threat is felt (Source: @SharghDaily/181805, @SharghDaily/181802).

Iran's FM Araghchi challenged Jordan's foreign minister publicly, questioning how long Iran should wait before responding to an aggressor who disrespects Arab sovereignty, and noted Arab airspace and waters were used in attacks (Source: @presstv/205484).

Satellite imagery analyzed by OSINT shows no runway mark at Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan on August 25, an apparent impact scar on September 2, and fresh repair work by September 3, matching Iran's September 1 attack claim (Source: @shin_persian/9445).

A Revolutionary Guard official told the New York Times that from June to present, 70-100 Hezbollah members including Iranian Quds Force advisors are trapped in tunnels around Ali Taher heights, with Iran and Hezbollah prioritizing evacuation but facing increasing difficulty as Israel wounds those attempting to retrieve equipment (Source: @mamlekate/104313).

Iran's military spokesperson stated the US has unlimited quantities of medium-to-high quality munitions and is in an unprecedented state of munitions production and stockpiling, while also providing munitions to Ukraine (Source: @VahidOnline/78217).
Reports indicate no anti-aircraft activity over Tehran, with Telegram claims to the contrary described as completely false by one source (Source: @shin_persian/9440).
israel: IDF announced operational control of Mount Ali Taher above and below ground, clearing the area of militants, with some militants killed and others escaping the area (Source: @inon_yttach/10014).

IDF Chief of Staff stated at a ceremony honoring forces that the army must be expanded, the service pool broadened, and adapted with advanced organization and capabilities to meet expanding missions (Source: @idf_telegram/25043).
Border police neutralized a militant wielding a knife near Shechem Gate in Jerusalem's Old City around 3:45 AM, with no casualties among forces (Source: @yediotnews25/134650).

Israel's Supreme Court cancelled the ultra-Orthodox draft-dodger arrest law 9-0, with 8 of 9 justices ruling the amendment unconstitutional and harmful to equality (Source: @amitsegal/64550, @yediotnews25/134645).

The Israel Free Movement party welcomed the Supreme Court decision, stating that no draft-dodder will receive immunity and no draft-dodger will sleep in peace while hundreds of thousands serve in the war (Source: @yediotnews25/134652).

Israel conveyed harsh criticism of the Lebanese army's performance to the US, demanding extensive weapons searches across all of south Lebanon or making withdrawal agreement significantly harder (Source: @pkpoi/143837).
Joint forces including fire fighters, volunteers, and all security forces achieved control over a fire threatening a settlement, as described by regional station commander (Source: @N12chat/224987).
gaza_west_bank: A stabbing attempt by a militant near Shechem Gate in Jerusalem's Old City was neutralized by border police around 3:45 AM, with no casualties among Israeli forces (Source: @yediotnews25/134650).

Security systems fear increased attempts at attacks against Israelis and Jews abroad backed by Iran's Quds Force and Hamas abroad, especially during the holiday period near the three-year anniversary of the October 7 attack (Source: @pkpoi/143831).
The Supreme Court's cancellation of the ultra-Orthodox arrest law was welcomed by civil rights groups as a step toward equality during wartime service (Source: @amitsegal/64550).
No specific Gaza Strip developments were reported in the available messages beyond the broader conflict context.
lebanon: Hezbollah's last stronghold at Tal Ali Taher and the underground Imad 4 facility fell to the Israeli army; Hezbollah refused to hand the site over to the Lebanese army and preferred transferring it to Israeli defense forces (Source: @kianmeli1/91514).

70-100 Hezbollah members including Iranian Quds Force advisors remain trapped in tunnels around Ali Taher heights, with Iran and Hezbollah prioritizing evacuation but facing increasing difficulty as Israel wounds those exiting (Source: @mamlekate/104313).

The US ambassador to Lebanon conveyed Israeli criticism of the Lebanese army's performance, demanding it conduct extensive searches for weapons across all south Lebanon areas, warning that failure to comply would make withdrawal agreement much harder (Source: @pkpoi/143837).
The Lebanese army reported a war remnant explosion in Froun town at 2:35, and fire was set around the town of Bani Hiyan (Source: @redlinkleb/40654, @rasedal3ado138e/388795).

Artillery shelling was reported in the area with direct maps circulating, though specific targets and casualties were not detailed in available messages (Source: @redlinkleb/40639, @redlinkleb/40666).
syria_iraq: ISIS claimed targeting an IRGC-backed PMU/Hashed Al Sha'abi vehicle in the Anbar desert in Iraq (Source: @shin_persian/9438).
A Revolutionary Guard ambush on Kurdish separatist forces occurred on the Iraq-Iran border in the Kurdistan region of northern Iraq (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/388800).

An Iraqi official responded to Jordan's foreign minister, questioning how long Iran should wait before responding to an aggressor who disrespects Arab sovereignty, noting Arab airspace was used in initial US attacks (Source: @naya_foriraq/89349).
An Iraqi news agency identified with the Iranian regime reported launches toward the Strait of Hormuz (Source: @New_security8200/203601).
No specific Syrian conflict developments were reported in the available messages.
gulf_states: Dubai and other Gulf states are experiencing severe tourism decline due to the US-Iran war: Dubai airport passenger traffic down 31% in the first half of the year, hotel occupancy dropped to 56%, and luxury real estate sales fell 59% (Source: @kianmeli1/91513).
Major events including the Bahrain Formula 1 race and Saudi Arabia's global esports World Cup have been delayed or cancelled due to the conflict (Source: @kianmeli1/91513).

The Wall Street Journal noted that Gulf states, viewed as safe regional locations for decades, now face changed global perceptions of active risk and investment due to the US-Iran war (Source: @kianmeli1/91513).

South Korea reversed its position on Hormuz deployment and is preparing military equipment including a maritime patrol aircraft, logistics support ship, or mine clearance unit to support freedom of navigation (Source: @kianmeli1/91515).

US officials told intermediaries that Washington wants to fully open the Strait of Hormuz regardless of any Iran-Oman agreement, having changed conditions after learning of progress in bilateral talks (Source: @naya_foriraq/89353).
Iran insists it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the US embargo is lifted, oil sales exemptions restored, and some frozen overseas assets accessed (Source: @naya_foriraq/89353).
At least five US fighter jets were reported active in the region according to simultaneous reports (Source: @rodast_omiddana/80294).
key_developments: US strikes confirmed on Iranian civilian targets in Sirik (wedding ceremony, child killed) and Kohestak (direct munition hit), with Iran's FM Araghchi publicly challenging Jordan over response timing (Source: @presstv/205485, @presstv/205486, @presstv/205484).

IDF achieved operational control of Mount Ali Taher as Hezbollah's last stronghold fell, with 70-100 Hezbollah members and Iranian Quds advisors trapped in underground tunnels (Source: @inon_yttach/10014, @mamlekate/104313).

Gulf states face severe economic disruption with Dubai airport traffic down 31%, hotel occupancy at 56%, and major events cancelled as the US-Iran war reshapes regional investment perceptions (Source: @kianmeli1/91513).

Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint: Iran refuses reopening without US sanctions relief while South Korea prepares military deployment and Washington demands full opening regardless of bilateral talks (Source: @naya_foriraq/89353, @kianmeli1/91515).

Iran's military pledged faster and more crushing preemptive operations against any Israeli aggression, citing destroyed enemy air defenses that now open missile and drone routes toward occupied territories (Source: @SharghDaily/181805).

Satellite imagery confirms an apparent impact at Jordan's Prince Hassan Air Base matching Iran's September 1 attack claim, with fresh repair work observed, suggesting Iranian missiles reached Israeli/Jordanian territory (Source: @shin_persian/9445).

ISIS claimed an attack on an IRGC-backed PMU vehicle in Iraq's Anbar desert while Revolutionary Guard ambushed Kurdish forces on the Iraq-Iran border, indicating expanding militant activity in the theater (Source: @shin_persian/9438, @rasedal3ado138e/388800).
sections.threat_assessment: The conflict has escalated into a multi-front war with confirmed US strikes on Iranian civilian targets and Iran's military openly threatening preemptive retaliation against any Israeli aggression. Hezbollah's collapse at Mount Ali Taher and the trapping of 70-100 fighters in tunnels suggests a critical degradation of Lebanon's resistance infrastructure. The Strait of Hormuz remains the most strategically significant flashpoint, with Iran refusing to reopen it without sanctions relief while the US demands full opening and South Korea prepares military deployment. The presence of at least five US fighter jets in the region and ISIS activity in Iraq's Anbar desert indicates the conflict is expanding in both geographic scope and militant actor involvement.
sections.regional_response: Gulf states are experiencing severe economic consequences with Dubai airport traffic down 31% and major events cancelled, signaling a fundamental shift in regional risk perception. Jordan's foreign minister publicly challenged Iran on response timing, while Iran's FM Araghchi countered by questioning Arab awareness of their airspace being used in US attacks. South Korea reversed its previous position and is now preparing military equipment for Hormuz deployment, indicating growing international involvement in securing the strait. The US has conveyed harsh criticism of Lebanon's army performance and demanded expanded weapons searches, suggesting Washington is pressuring Beirut to meet Israeli security conditions before any withdrawal agreement.
sections.intelligence_notes: Satellite imagery analysis confirms an apparent impact scar at Jordan's Prince Hassan Air Base dated September 2, matching Iran's claimed September 1 attack timeline, with fresh repair work by September 3, indicating Iranian missiles may have reached beyond their intended targets. A Revolutionary Guard official's disclosure to the New York Times about 70-100 trapped Hezbollah members and Quds advisors in Ali Taher tunnels provides rare insight into the scale of Iranian entanglement in Lebanon. Iran's claim of unlimited munitions production and stockpiling, combined with reports of unprecedented manufacturing rates, suggests sustained operational capacity. The Iraqi news agency reporting launches toward Hormuz and ISIS claiming attacks on IRGC-backed forces in Anbar indicate the conflict is generating secondary threats across Iraq.
